subject: AHM2's CAR models in NIMBLE (and in parallel)

messages.author: 72444bb824190d51
messages.subject: AHM2's CAR models in NIMBLE (and in parallel)
parts:
Kéry & Royle (2021) Applied Hierarchical Modeling Vol.2 (AHM2) includes 5 spatial auto-regressive CAR models, 2 in chapter 3 and 3 in chapter 9. The code is available at the AHM_code GitHub repository.

Since JAGS will not do spatial auto-correlation models, these were coded in good ol' WinBUGS 1.4. WinBUGS is specific to the Windows OS. It is no longer maintained, and is not guaranteed to work on future Windows upgrades. The relatively new NIMBLE package will do spatial models, and I have 'translated' the WinBUGS code to run with nimble::nimbleMCMC. See the files tagged "..._nimble.R" here and here.

These models mix poorly and long runs are required, taking up to 5 days. It makes sense to run chains in parallel and to use as many cores as possible. Unlike jagsUI::jags, neither R2WinBUGS::bugs nor nimble::nimbleMCMC has built-in capability for parallel processing. Multiple instances can, however, be run in parallel using the CRAN package foreach. I've added code to implement this to the scripts in the AHM_code repository. See more information on using foreach here.

The model in section 9.5 caused problems. In WinBUGS, it often throws an error, "Undefined real result". Kéry & Royle advise retrying multiple times. With foreach, with the argument .errorhandling='remove', it's easy to discard chains that throw errors and recover the results of those that run properly.

With this model, NIMBLE does not throw an error but prints a warning, "logProb is -Inf". It runs, but some of the random walk samplers are stuck at their starting values (with acceptance rate 0). The problem occurs when several of the starting values generated automatically by NIMBLE are far out in the tails of the posterior distribution, so that the probability of the model is effectively zero.

I identified and discarded the "stuck" chains and looked at the posterior distributions of the top-level stochastic nodes from those that worked. Based on that information, I added values to the inits function, with random draws from uniform distributions somewhat wider than the CrIs of the posteriors. The model than ran properly. More details and diagnostic plots are here.

messages.author: 72444bb824190d51
messages.subject: Re: AHM2's CAR models in NIMBLE (and in parallel)
parts:
The comment about runs "taking up to 5 days" refers to the original WinBUGS code (specifically the model in section 3.4.5). With the same number of iterations and chains in series, NIMBLE would take about 15 hours. With more, shorter chains run in parallel and with less (but still adequate) burn-in, the time could be reduced below 2hrs.

NIMBLE is  much faster than WinBUGS for these models.
